input: Write a short play for my nephew's school performance

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The length and number of scenes directly shapes how much content needs to be written and how complex the structure should be.
The number of cast members and their age group determines how many speaking roles to write and how complex the dialogue and acting demands should be.
The theme, subject, or occasion of the performance (e.g. holiday, history lesson, moral story) defines the entire premise of the play.
A hard time limit on the performance determines how long the script can be and how much action can fit in.
The desired tone — whether funny, dramatic, educational, or heartwarming — shapes every line of dialogue and stage direction.
Knowing whether there are staging or prop limitations (e.g. no costumes, simple set) affects what scenes and actions can realistically be written in.
Understanding what role the nephew plays (lead, ensemble, specific character type) ensures the script is tailored so he has the right presence and lines.

gold.taskTitle: Write a short play for nephew's school performance
gold.taskDescription: Write an original short play suitable for a school performance involving the user's nephew.

questions.title: What is the play's theme or subject meant to be?
questions.description: Identify the central topic, story, or occasion driving the play — e.g. a fairy tale, a historical event, a moral lesson, a holiday celebration.

questions.title: How long should the performance run?
questions.description: Establish the target runtime in minutes to determine the appropriate script length and pacing.

questions.title: How many students will be in the cast?
questions.description: Determine the total number of performers so the right number of speaking and non-speaking roles can be written.

questions.title: What age group are the student performers?
questions.description: Knowing the performers' ages guides the complexity of vocabulary, dialogue length, and acting demands in the script.

questions.title: Should the tone be funny, serious, or educational?
questions.description: Pin down the desired mood and style of the play so the writing voice, humour level, and dramatic weight are appropriately calibrated.

questions.title: What kind of role does your nephew play?
questions.description: Clarify whether the nephew has a lead role, a specific character type, or is part of an ensemble, so his part can be written with the right prominence and lines.

questions.title: Are there any staging or prop limitations to keep in mind?
questions.description: Understand physical constraints of the performance space — such as no elaborate costumes, a bare stage, or limited props — to ensure scenes are stageable.
